_schema: EVERY WORD THE PLAYER READS. dialogue.js owns none of it. A NODE is { speaker, lines[], choices[], effects, next, if, else }. LINES are strings or { text, speaker, name, expr, if, effects } — expr picks assets/characters/<portrait>/expr-<expr>.png for that ONE line and silently falls back to bust.png where the art does not exist yet, so a mood can be written before it is drawn. CONDITIONS read GS.state.flags and nothing else: "flag", "notFlag", "flagIs", "flagAtLeast", "hasItem", "goldAtLeast", and "all"/"any"/"not" to combine them; a bare string is shorthand for { flag: ... }. A node whose `if` fails falls through to its `else`, which is how first-meeting and repeat-visit versions of the same conversation live under one entry point. EFFECTS write the same store: setFlags, incFlags, giveItem/giveQty, gold — and `shop`, which hands the player to shops.json AFTER the window closes, so a keeper greets you and then opens the counter instead of both talking at once. CHOICES are { text, to, if, effects }; `to: null` ends the conversation. Nodes are namespaced <who>.<what> so a quest can add branches without colliding.
_voice: Written to docs/VOICES.md, which is law. Dellhollow register (docs/chapter2-dellhollow-script.md): a normal flameless town, four hundred years old, holding together on nothing but people. No lamp-lore, no Heartlight, no mystery — rivers, weather, bread, rope, manners. NOBODY IN THIS FILE SAYS THE WORD 'AFRAID': the town is POLITE to its river and corrects anyone who suggests otherwise. Aphorism budget is one per conversation from a licensed source — Odessa spends hers at the lockhead, Creel's trade-observations are inside his own budget, and nobody else gets one. Lines are 8-18 words, two sentences at most. These are ambient day-in-the-life lines: nobody here carries a plot fact, and nothing here contradicts or pre-empts the chapter script.
_embVoice: EMBERBROOK AMBIENT LINES START HERE, and they are a different register from the Dellhollow block above: a warm, close, three-hundred-year-old home village on the evening of its own festival, where Dellhollow is a working river town holding together on manners. THE HARD RULE IS THE SAME AND STRICTER — nobody here carries a plot fact and nothing here pre-empts public/js/chapter1.js, which is SHIPPED content that owns every beat of Emberwake. So: bread, bunting, washing, the walk up to the square, a cat. No Heartlight, no Kindling Hour, no lamps-lore, no Hush, no foreshadowing — the words a villager would use about a Thursday that happens to be the nicest night of the year. Voice per docs/VOICES.md; 8-18 words, two sentences at most. As of the 2026-08-02 style pass chapter1.js HAS had its voice pass and every box in this file is measured by tools/dialogue_style.mjs alongside it; docs/exemplars.md is the ratified example set to match.
_doc_southroad: THE WHISPERWOOD ROAD REFUSES ITSELF (PT-20260803-002/-008). The arrival clearing's south exit is a real edge with a real prompt, and until Chapter One is done it plays one of these instead of transitioning — public/townmap/emberbrook.map.json exit 'valley-road-south' names this node under `denyDialogue`, tools/scenegraph_derive.mjs carries it onto the edge as `deny`, and play3d.html's sgDenied()/sgSpeakDenial() spend it. It is NOT a beat: no flag is written, no ledger entry is made, nobody is moved. It is the character declining, which is the only shape of 'you cannot go that way' this project allows. THE ENTRY NODE BRANCHES ON WHOSE BODY IT IS: during ch1.lake.handoff..ch1.meet the player carries Lake (story.ch1.lake-pov set, story.ch1.met not yet), and a Vesper line out of Lake's mouth on his own lamp round is the defect this branch exists to avoid.

defaults._players: The party. dialogue.js anchors these speakers' cut-ins on the RIGHT of the box, opposite the NPC, and uses the first of them as the voice of a choice list (user ruling 2026-08-01: the player characters get a portrait on every beat the player speaks, choices included). A node may name a different `chooser`.

_busts: EVERY SPEAKER HAS A FACE (user ruling, 2026-08-01: 'every time you speak to somebody, they should have an appropriate character bust'). `portrait` is now WRITTEN OUT for every entry rather than left to dialogue.js's default-to-the-id, because it is no longer always the id: a background villager wears an ARCHETYPE bust (villager-woman, villager-man, elder-woman, fisher, child-girl, child-boy, innkeeper) the same way he wears one of the four rigged GLBs — borrowed art, worn as somebody else's coat, and the archetype id in this column is the whole record of the loan. The ten Dellhollow extras the scripts called 'nameplate-only' (Hobb, Pell, Sorrel, Creel, Nib, and the eel-wife, boatwright and three keepers) were drawn on 2026-08-01 by tools/gen-character.mjs --only key,bust and now carry their own; that supersedes the sprite-first note in chapter2-expansion-script.md §b. `portrait: false` SURVIVES FOR EXACTLY ONE SPEAKER, `system`, which is the narrator channel and not a person — tools/dialogue_test.mjs allows that one id and FAILS THE BUILD on any other speaker without a bust file on disk.

lines.text: Harbormistress. You'll be the stranger — the quay's told me twice already, with improvements.
Say your business plain. I've a town of idle boats to keep out of trouble.
Mm.
The kettle's on at the cookhouse. Go and be warm somewhere.
Five locks step this water down the gorge. The fifth is shut, and it stays shut.
The river asked for a season. The town gave it one.
My ruling stands as posted. Argue with the board, not with me.
The Lockhead. I stand here, I read the water, and I say what passes.
Mind the rail. It's older than your grandmother and a good deal prouder.
Pell does. Oil, wick, ladder — and one complaint per lamp, paid in advance.
He's never once missed a noon. Quote me on it — he'll pretend not to hear.
You're the stranger! Whole quay says so — and the quay says everything, mostly wrong.
Maren. Pilot, when anybody lets me. Water-eye, always.
Tide's slack, boat's tied, nobody needs me. Ask me anything, I'll answer it twice.
Lock Five. Deepest chamber on the river, and the water in it never hurries.
I've been down it ten times. Ma says nine, and Ma is wrong for once.
Locks worked. Charcoal, so it washes — I redraw them every morning.
It's not sad. It's bookkeeping.
It's the house's. Tarred every winter, whether anyone rows it or not.
Don't step in her with dry boots on. That's not a rule, it's just correct.

hobb.hail.speaker: hobb
lines: Don't lean on anything. Everything here is either hot, wet, or mine.
Forty ton of pumpkins, going soft. In elegant rows.
Nineteen days in this queue. It has bunting now, and we've named the seagulls.
"Cut them for pie," my wife says. Madam, there is no fair for a November pumpkin.

hobb.again.speaker: hobb
lines: Still here. Still soft. Don't ask which of us I mean.

hobb.round.speaker: hobb
lines: Round. Round WHAT, exactly — the cliff? There's one road out of this gorge and it's wet.
You want north, so do forty ton of pumpkins. Get in the queue — it's a patient one.

hobb.sorry.speaker: hobb
lines: Don't be sorry, be useful— no. No, forgive me. Nobody's useful against the river.
First thing you learn up here. Last thing you believe.

lines.text: Watchman. Night shift. It is presently day, which is why I'm holding a wick-knife and a grudge.
Every wick, every noon, so they burn every night. That's the whole trade.
No ceremony to it, friend. Oil goes in, light comes out.
And I'd thank the town to remember who carries the ladder.
Sleep's for the day shift — which is now. Which is the grudge.
Two hundred and six, counting the strings over the water. I don't count those out loud.
One ladder. One me. You do the sum and then you understand my face.

pell.nights.speaker: pell

lines.text: Quiet enough. Gulls arguing, water working, somebody laughing at the cookhouse too late.

lines: A town with its lamps lit doesn't need much watching. That's the point of the lamps.

sorrel.hail.speaker: sorrel
lines: Mind the drip-line, love. Wash overhead, bread underhand.
Half-loaf's a penny. Whole loaf's a penny and a look at your cat.
Nineteen days of stuck boats buying my bread. My ovens haven't cooled since.
Don't tell the harbormistress which way I'm praying.

sorrel.again.speaker: sorrel
lines: Half-loaf's still a penny. The cat's credit is good.

choices.text: Where do I find the shops?

sorrel.bunting.speaker: sorrel
lines: Regatta. Eleven years back, and nobody's ever taken it down.
It's not anybody's job, love. That's exactly why it's still up.

sorrel.shops.speaker: sorrel
lines: Up the stair to the Shelf. Chandler, then the smith, then the armorer, all in a row.
Two of them hang out over the gorge on brackets. Buy fast and don't look down.

creel.hail.speaker: creel
lines: Four hundred years of stairs, stranger. The town's knees give out before the timber does.
I've spliced rope on this deck since I was the boy with the gulls.
And there's always a boy with the gulls.

creel.again.speaker: creel
lines: Mind your feet going down. Coming up, mind everything else.

creel.bridges.speaker: creel
lines: Sound as sermons. I splice what they hang from, so I'd know first.
Rope tells you before it goes. So do most things, if you're the sort that listens.

creel.splice.speaker: creel
lines: Drying line. Somebody's wash came down in the wind and somebody blamed the wind.
It was the splice. It's always the splice — and I'll not say whose.

nib.hail.speaker: nib

lines.text: That one's Bailiff, that one's Soup. The big one's called the Harbormistress.
Don't TELL the harbormistress.

lines: You're littler than the quay said.

lines.text: Soup! SOUP! …He knows his name. He just doesn't respect it.

choices.text: Who's in charge of the gulls?

nib.office.speaker: nib

lines.text: Me. Nobody said so, but nobody else does it, so it's me.

lines: They go in order, biggest at the top. Everybody slides down one when a bigger one lands.

nib.dock.speaker: nib
lines: Eels. Then more eels. Then the deep stairs, and you're not allowed up them.

lines.text: I'm not allowed either. That's different, because I already went.
Two for a penny! Three if you carry them, and no, I won't skin them for you.
You weren't buying. I priced you anyway — it's the principle of the stall.
That cat's been fed twice today. We have an understanding and no witnesses.
Still two for a penny. The river hasn't changed its mind and neither have I.
Boats stopped, mouths didn't. Best nineteen days I've had and I'll deny saying it.
Ask me in the spring and I'll tell you it was a hardship. It will be true by then.

boatwright.hail.speaker: boatwright

lines.text: Mind the pitch kettle. It's hot, it's mine, and it doesn't care which.

lines: Two hulls in frames, one waiting on oak. Nothing goes back in the water dry.

lines.text: Nineteen days of stopped boats is nineteen days of stopped boats getting mended.
Still ribs and tar. Come back when there's a hull worth looking at.

choices.text: How long does a hull take?
I'll keep out of the way.

lines.text: Frames in a week, planking in a month. Trust in about ten years.
You don't build a boat fast up here. The river checks your work personally.

boatwright.smell.speaker: boatwright
lines: Pitch. You'll taste it for a day and then you'll stop noticing forever.

lines.text: Half this town smells of tar and the other half married into it.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (A cat is sitting at the eel-stall with the composure of a paying customer. He does not look up.)

lines.speaker: mochi
lines.text: Mrrp.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (The eel-wife has already fed him twice. Neither of them has admitted it.)

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (He has moved four inches into the sun and filed the move as a full day's work.)

lines.speaker: mochi
lines.text: Mrrp.

chandler.hail.speaker: chandler
lines: Chandlery. Oil, rope, pitch, and whatever else the river takes off you.

lines.text: Half this floor hangs over the gorge on brackets. It's held ninety years. Don't jump.
Oil's fresh, rope's dry, floor's still up. Same as yesterday.
Look all you like. Everyone leaves with rope eventually.

weaponsmith.hail.speaker: weaponsmith
lines: Nothing here's a sword. Boat-hooks, cudgels, staves — river tools that argue back.
Everything on this wall has a day job. That's what makes it honest.

weaponsmith.again.speaker: weaponsmith
lines: Back again. Everyone ends up buying the hook.

weaponsmith.looking.speaker: weaponsmith
lines: Suit yourself. Try the balance on the staff before you decide you're the walking sort.

armorer.hail.speaker: armorer
lines: Oilskin and quilting. Up here the weather hits you harder than anything else will.
Dry is armor. Anyone who says different has never worked a gorge in November.

armorer.again.speaker: armorer
lines: Still raining somewhere. Still selling coats.

armorer.looking.speaker: armorer
lines: Look while it's dry. You'll come back when it isn't.

del.deckhand.hail.speaker: del.deckhand
lines: Nineteen days ashore. I've read that notice board twice and it hasn't improved.

lines.text: Three shops on this street, and I've been in all of them. I've bought a whistle.

del.deckhand.again.speaker: del.deckhand
lines: Still moored. Still walking. The street's shorter than it was yesterday.

del.netmender.hail.speaker: del.netmender
lines: Mind the racks. Everything on this deck is drying and everything drips.
A net comes back wrong and I put it right. That's the whole of it.

del.netmender.again.speaker: del.netmender
lines: Same net. Bigger hole than I said it was.

del.stairgran.hail.speaker: del.stairgran
lines: Road's flat as far as my door. Past it, it's four hundred years of steps.
Go on down, love. I'll be here — I'm always here now.

del.stairgran.again.speaker: del.stairgran
lines: Down's easy. Everyone finds that out coming back up.

del.quayfisher.hail.speaker: del.quayfisher
lines: Locks shut, water's still. Best fishing I've had in a year and I can't say so out loud.
Whatever I land goes to the stall down there. She prices it, and I don't argue.

del.quayfisher.again.speaker: del.quayfisher
lines: Two since we spoke. Don't tell her, she'll have heard already.

del.gullgirl.hail.speaker: del.gullgirl

lines.text: That's my stick. I found it — don't ask where, it was in the river.

lines: The boy on the dock says he runs the gulls. He doesn't run anything.

lines.text: Still my stick.

rowan.hail.speaker: rowan
lines: Ah — a face I'd remember. And I would, I keep the book on faces.
They put me on the dais every year and every year I say I don't run anything.

lines.text: Still not running it. Still standing where they put me.

choices.text: What are you keeping track of?

lines.text: Forty years of who owes whom a hand. Nobody has ever asked to see it.
That's the trick of a ledger in a village. Keeping it is the whole of the work.

rowan.night.speaker: rowan
lines: Every year. Same square, same bunting, and I've never once got the knot right.

poppy.hail.speaker: poppy
lines: Window's open, so I'm open. Mind the sill, it's hot on this side.
Fourth tray today. Burnt my thumb on the first one, same as every morning.

lines.text: Still warm. Won't be by the time you've decided.

poppy.tray.speaker: poppy
lines: Honeybuns. Under the cloth so the children have to ask, which is half the fun.

lines.text: Up at four, and I'll be up at four tomorrow. It's a good complaint to have.

mara.hail.speaker: mara
lines: Evening. Don't mind him — he's mine, and he's on his eleventh lap of this square.

lines.text: He'll tell you about the stick. Let him, it's shorter than you'd think.
Twelfth lap. I've stopped counting out loud.

choices.text: He's got a lot of energy.

mara.pip.speaker: mara
lines: He has one speed and it isn't mine. I gave up trying to match it years ago.

mara.square.speaker: mara
lines: It holds the whole village when it has to. Tonight it will have to.

pip.hail.speaker: pip
lines: Are you new? You're new — I can tell, because I know everyone and I don't know you.
This is my stick, and it's the good one. I have others but they're not this one.

lines.text: Still the good one. I checked.

pip.stick.speaker: pip
lines: I KNOW. Everyone says it's a stick. It is, but that's not the point of it.

lines.text: Mum's right there. That counts. She says it counts when she's the one saying it.

finn.hail.speaker: finn
lines: Careful on the boards, they're greener than they look. Everything here is.

lines.text: Nothing biting. Hasn't all week. I come down anyway, that's the arrangement.

finn.again.speaker: finn
lines: Still nothing. Still here. Don't read anything into it.

choices.text: Why come down if nothing's biting?

finn.why.speaker: finn
lines: Because the pond's there and I'm here. You'd want a better reason, and I haven't got one.

lines.text: Half the winter, hanging. Everyone's very fond of me in February.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (A cat is sitting on the waystone. He was sitting on it before you came round the bend, and his position on the subject has not changed.)

lines.speaker: mochi
lines.text: Mrrp.

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (He looks at the road ahead of you, and then at you, in that order.)

lines.speaker: system
lines.text: (Still the waystone, still the cat. He has moved four inches into the last of the sun.)

emb.miller.hail.speaker: emb.miller
lines: Wheel's down for the night. First time this month it's stopped before I did.
Whole village walks past this door and not one of them hears it until it's off.

emb.miller.again.speaker: emb.miller
lines: Quiet, isn't it. Takes about a day to stop noticing.

lines.text: Evening. I'd walk up with you but I'm carrying a dish and it's not a steady one.
Whole lane's going up. You can tell by the doors — none of them shut properly.
Still carrying it. Getting there.

emb.townsfolk.hail.speaker: emb.townsfolk
lines: In before dark, that's the rule. Damp gets into a sheet and never quite leaves.
Go on up, love, they'll all be up there. I'll come when the line's empty.

emb.townsfolk.again.speaker: emb.townsfolk
lines: Two more and I'm done. It's always two more.

lines.text: You can't ring it. I asked. You have to be Elder Rowan or the bell falls on you.
That's not true but he said it, so it's a bit true.
Still can't ring it. I've been checking.

emb.boy.hail.speaker: emb.boy
lines: This is Pip's. I'm allowed in it but only when he's here, and he isn't.

lines.text: So I'm waiting. That's allowed — it's the main thing you can do at a den.
Still not here. I've got all evening.

emb.innkeep.hail.speaker: emb.innkeep

lines.text: Come in, then. Two rooms and a fire, and tonight nobody wants any of the three.

lines: They're all up at the square. I'll go when the kettle's off and not before.

lines.text: Kettle's still on. It's a very slow kettle tonight.

emb.shopkeep.hail.speaker: emb.shopkeep
lines: Preserves, twine, lamp oil. Everything a person needs and nothing anyone wants.
Not selling tonight, mind — nobody sells tonight. Take what you need and tell me after.

emb.shopkeep.again.speaker: emb.shopkeep
lines: Still open. Still not selling. It's a fine distinction and it's mine.

lines.text: (Nothing down there but the Whisperwood. My lamps are the other way.)
(South is eleven days of road I've surveyed. The lights north aren't on any map I carry.)

del.innkeep.hail.speaker: del.innkeep
lines: Beds are upstairs and all of them are full. Nineteen days of crews and nowhere to send them.
You can have the bench by the fire. It's warm, it's free, and it's taken at nine.

del.innkeep.again.speaker: del.innkeep
lines: Bench is still by the fire. Still taken at nine.

del.inn.bargeman.hail.speaker: del.inn.bargeman
lines: Ashore since the locks shut. I've drunk this cellar dry in small honest amounts.
My boat's third in the queue. Third of forty, and I've stopped saying that out loud.

del.inn.bargeman.again.speaker: del.inn.bargeman
lines: Still third. Ask me tomorrow and it'll still be third.

del.inn.lodger.hail.speaker: del.inn.lodger
lines: That's my bag by the stair. It's been packed since the locks shut.
I'm not carrying it up again. If the water moves, I want to hear it first.

del.inn.lodger.again.speaker: del.inn.lodger
lines: Bag's still packed by the stair. So am I.

del.cook.hail.speaker: del.cook
lines: Mind the range, it spits. Everything in this room is hotter than it looks.
Two hundred meals a day when the locks run. Ninety now, and I still start at four.

del.cook.again.speaker: del.cook
lines: Pot's on. It's always on — that's the job.

del.cookhouse.bargeman.hail.speaker: del.cookhouse.bargeman
lines: Stew and a bit of bread. Same as yesterday, and I'm not complaining.
Cheaper than the inn and you eat standing up. Crews work that out by day three.

del.cookhouse.bargeman.again.speaker: del.cookhouse.bargeman
lines: Still waiting on the hatch. She serves in her own order.

del.cookhouse.boy.hail.speaker: del.cookhouse.boy
lines: I get the crusts when the pot's scraped. That's a wage, my mam says.
You can sit there. Nobody's using it and I won't tell.

del.cookhouse.boy.again.speaker: del.cookhouse.boy
lines: Crusts aren't ready. Come back when the pot's down.

del.yard.apprentice.hail.speaker: del.yard.apprentice
lines: I fetch, I hold, and I don't touch the adze. Two years of that so far.
The boatwright's down at the kettle. Shout if you want him, he won't hear you.

del.yard.apprentice.again.speaker: del.yard.apprentice
lines: Still holding things. He'll want the mallet in a minute.

del.yard.caulker.hail.speaker: del.yard.caulker
lines: Mind your feet round the frames. Oakum, mallet, and a seam that takes me all day.
Every hull in this yard leaks somewhere. Mine's this one, and it's winning.

del.yard.caulker.again.speaker: del.yard.caulker
lines: Same seam as yesterday. Half a day left in it, I reckon.
